minor.issue: Spec requires items to include {id, name, role_name}; implementation only returns {id, name} because db.users docs don't carry a denormalised role_name field (projection asks for it but it is null → omitted). Add a role_name lookup (join roles collection or write it on user upsert).

ui_bugs.issue: After POST /customers succeeds (201), the component immediately calls api.patch(`/customers/{id}/profile`, prof) WITHOUT a `version` field (CustomerForm.jsx line 52). The axios interceptor in lib/api.js rejects every PATCH without body.version (line 28-30), so a toast fires 'PATCH /customers/.../profile requires a version (optimistic concurrency)' and the user is NOT navigated to Customer 360. The customer record IS created (visible on next list refresh) but profile fields (salutation_id, state_id, city_id, occupation_id, rm_user_id, preferences, segments, consent, residency/nationality) are NEVER persisted. Fix: include `version: r.data.version ?? 0` in the profile PATCH body, or special-case /profile paths in the api.js interceptor.

critical_code_review_comments: lib/api.js:28-30 rejects *every* PATCH without body.version. CustomerForm's post-create profile PATCH violates this contract because new resources start at version 0 but the create response is spread into `r.data` and `version` isn't threaded into the follow-up call. The pattern 'POST then PATCH /profile' happens only for /customers/new — either stop making two calls (accept the whole profile in POST /customers) or always pass version from r.data. The current UX silently loses salutation/state/city/occupation/residency/nationality/segments/preferences on first save.
routers/customers.py rm-options projection asks for role_name but seeded users don't carry it. Easiest fix: when listing, $lookup from roles by role_id (or add migration to write role_name on users).
routers/customers.py GET /api/customers/{customer_id} uses `get_or_404` on the id column only; add a fallback lookup by customer_code so FE routes that use codes don't 404.

Combined ledger definition drift: services/ledgers.customer_ledgers builds Combined by summing all three buckets including other_charges; Customer 360 hero stats come from a different aggregation (bookings.summary) that excludes charges. Pick one source of truth.

rca of the issue: RCA — Customer create BLOCKER: The frontend axios interceptor (/app/frontend/src/lib/api.js lines 24-32) enforces 'all PATCH requests must carry body.version' as a client-side optimistic-concurrency guard. CustomerForm.submit (/app/frontend/src/pages/v2/CustomerForm.jsx line 49-52) performs POST /customers, then calls PATCH /customers/{cid}/profile with a payload built only from catalogue ids — no `version` key. The interceptor rejects before the request leaves the browser, raising 'PATCH /customers/{id}/profile requires a version (optimistic concurrency)'. The catch block fires toast.error and the nav(`/customers/{cid}`) line never runs. Backend state: customer row inserted with name/phone/pan/aadhaar + address_current from the POST body, but every catalogue-driven profile field (salutation_id, state_id, city_id, occupation_id, residency_id, nationality_id, segment_ids, rm_user_id, preferences, consent) remains unset because the PATCH never arrived. Mitigation: `version: r.data.version ?? 0` (one line). Longer-term: either collapse profile fields into the create payload (POST /customers accepts them), or exempt /profile paths from the version-required rule.
